title: Prove the sharp half-shift Gaussian inverse lower envelope (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped written proof with exact finite corroboration. For every finite normalized Gaussian section at either half-shift endpoint, determine its exact inverse-norm infimum over the Gaussian scale:

```text
T[i,j] = q^((j-i)^2-epsilon(j-i)),  0<q<1, epsilon=+1 or -1
inf_q ||T^(-1)||_2 = 1/(2 sin(pi/(4N+2))).
```

For N>=2 every positive q gives a strictly larger norm; q tending to zero approaches the infimum. At N=1 the norm is one. The proof compares the whole positive checkerboard inverse with the triangular all-ones matrix and uses its classical singular value. This answers the scale-uniform part of Jose Manuel / jmbarrancoml's #4193 finite-cap sharpness question. The exact norm at fixed q remains open.

Only six files in `research/gaussian-half-shift-envelope/` are added. The contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit #4193 for the question and finite-cap framework; Vlado Vojdanovski / #1673 for the cited q-LDU factors; Jeremy Kothe and the #1758 contributors for the shifted Gaussian lineage; Cinna Davis for the later caller; and Nick Petalas #5150/#6459 for related lower and upper results. No priority is claimed for the classical triangular singular values or positivity argument. No predecessor scientific verifier is replayed.

[Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19538492). Canonical base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`, priority revision 8, selected #7000 unchanged.

## Evidence

The cited predecessor supplies finite-cap upper bounds and leaves sharpness open. The new written proof supplies the exact scale-uniform lower envelope and an approaching family.

Local CPython 3.12.15, standard library only:

- 80 literal rational endpoint matrices and 2,040 inverse entries; both inverse products and the new triangular domination pass. All 70 nontrivial-size cases have a strict diagonal witness.
- 32 complete Laurent-polynomial characteristic identities and eight triangular inverse pairs pass without floating-point trigonometry.
- 28 small-scale matrices and 21 strict decreases in their exact squared Frobenius errors pass. Ten invalid inputs reject and five semantic control groups pass.
- Warning-strict normal and optimized direct checks produce identical hash-bound receipts, each in under one second locally. Both registered commands pass; the complete registered replay takes under one second. These are validation durations, not speedup claims.
- In-memory source compilation, staged whitespace inspection and committed-byte/source-history checks pass at `f1401fd8618394634c4f2a2171a668ba5f6915c2`.

Reproduce from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/gaussian-half-shift-envelope/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/gaussian-half-shift-envelope/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/gaussian-half-shift-envelope
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/gaussian-half-shift-envelope --check-source-history
```

Substitute another CPython 3.12 interpreter path elsewhere. Expected markers are `PASS_GAUSSIAN_HALF_SHIFT_ENVELOPE`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`. Receipts are generated from the current six file hashes; none is handwritten or committed.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The universal statement relies on the written proof and cited q-LDU premise. Finite checks corroborate it. The result is an exact infimum over q, not the norm at a prescribed positive q. Earlier related linear-growth consequences retain their credit.

No interior-shift lower envelope, fixed-q leading coefficient, production normalization/gauges, rounded inverse, physical execution, native/compiler/stock/tape invoice, supplier admission, new kappa or complete multiplication theorem is supplied. All five selected framework assumptions remain. Lean, Docker, predecessor scientific suites, selected full cold replay and separate type/lint analysis are unrun. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Related open work

No open PR studying this normalized constant-shift half-endpoint infimum surfaced in the current search. The cached full search covered 477 open PR bodies; fresh current PR metadata and handoff claims were checked before committing. Sparse notes, arbitrary historical diffs and unpublished work remain coverage limits.

- #3910 bounds the physical Gaussian forward row mass and its input contract; this contribution bounds a finite Toeplitz inverse norm in a different normalization.
- #371 accounts for final-grid rounding in a Gaussian block enclosure; this contribution concerns exact matrix inverses and supplies no rounding policy.

Merged #4193 supplies the cited factors and upper estimate. Merged #6459 improves an upper envelope; #5150 and #6483 concern varying-phase boundary cells. No predecessor census or numerical comparison was run for this contribution.

The completion refresh examined this account's open contributions created since the CLAIM: #7178, #7179 and #7181 through #7187. They concern shell growth, Coxeter tariffs, Clifford sectors, cube-zero lifts, radical tariffs, rational headers, block signatures and samplers. None studies this constant-shift Gaussian inverse envelope or computes a conflicting shared value. No extra scientific comparison computations were run.

## Open next questions

- Determine the sharp leading coefficient at fixed positive q as N grows. Start with the positive inverse in the bulk upper triangle; boundary and near-diagonal control remain missing.
- Determine the finite-size crossover as a shift approaches a half. Start with the geometrically decaying triangle under exact diagonal conjugation; justify the two-parameter limit before using it in a caller.
